#### Clase `_Finder` (Línea 84)
- **Docstring:** _Base class that exposes functionality for module/package finders_
- **Métodos:**
  - `def find(cls, where, exclude, include)` (Línea 91): Return a list of all Python items (packages or modules, depending on
the finder implementation) found within directory ``where``.

``where`` is the root directory which will be searched.
It should be supplied as a "cross-platform" (i.e. URL-style) path;
it will be converted to the appropriate local path syntax.

``exclude`` is a sequence of names to exclude; ``*`` can be used
as a wildcard in the names.
When finding packages, ``foo.*`` will exclude all subpackages of ``foo``
(but not ``foo`` itself).

``include`` is a sequence of names to include.
If it's specified, only the named items will be included.
If it's not specified, all found items will be included.
``include`` can contain shell style wildcard patterns just like
``exclude``.
  - `def _find_iter(cls, where, exclude, include)` (Línea 126): Sin docstring.

#### Clase `ConfigDiscovery` (Línea 298)
- **Docstring:** _Fill-in metadata and options that can be automatically derived
(from other metadata/options, the file system or conventions)_
- **Métodos:**
  - `def __init__(self, distribution)` (Línea 303): Sin docstring.
  - `def _disable(self)` (Línea 309): Internal API to disable automatic discovery
  - `def _ignore_ext_modules(self)` (Línea 313): Internal API to disregard ext_modules.

Normally auto-discovery would not be triggered if ``ext_modules`` are set
(this is done for backward compatibility with existing packages relying on
``setup.py`` or ``setup.cfg``). However, ``setuptools`` can call this function
to ignore given ``ext_modules`` and proceed with the auto-discovery if
``packages`` and ``py_modules`` are not given (e.g. when using pyproject.toml
metadata).
  - `def _root_dir(self)` (Línea 326): Sin docstring.
  - `def _package_dir(self)` (Línea 331): Sin docstring.
  - `def __call__(self, force, name, ignore_ext_modules)` (Línea 336): Automatically discover missing configuration fields
and modifies the given ``distribution`` object in-place.

Note that by default this will only have an effect the first time the
``ConfigDiscovery`` object is called.

To repeatedly invoke automatic discovery (e.g. when the project
directory changes), please use ``force=True`` (or create a new
``ConfigDiscovery`` instance).
  - `def _explicitly_specified(self, ignore_ext_modules)` (Línea 359): ``True`` if the user has specified some form of package/module listing
  - `def _analyse_package_layout(self, ignore_ext_modules)` (Línea 372): Sin docstring.
  - `def _analyse_explicit_layout(self)` (Línea 390): The user can explicitly give a package layout via ``package_dir``
  - `def _analyse_src_layout(self)` (Línea 408): Try to find all packages or modules under the ``src`` directory
(or anything pointed by ``package_dir[""]``).

The "src-layout" is relatively safe for automatic discovery.
We assume that everything within is meant to be included in the
distribution.

If ``package_dir[""]`` is not given, but the ``src`` directory exists,
this function will set ``package_dir[""] = "src"``.
  - `def _analyse_flat_layout(self)` (Línea 433): Try to find all packages and modules under the project root.

Since the ``flat-layout`` is more dangerous in terms of accidentally including
extra files/directories, this function is more conservative and will raise an
error if multiple packages or modules are found.

This assumes that multi-package dists are uncommon and refuse to support that
use case in order to be able to prevent unintended errors.
  - `def _analyse_flat_packages(self)` (Línea 446): Sin docstring.
  - `def _analyse_flat_modules(self)` (Línea 453): Sin docstring.
  - `def _ensure_no_accidental_inclusion(self, detected, kind)` (Línea 459): Sin docstring.
  - `def analyse_name(self)` (Línea 482): The packages/modules are the essential contribution of the author.
Therefore the name of the distribution can be derived from them.
  - `def _find_name_single_package_or_module(self)` (Línea 499): Exactly one module or package
  - `def _find_name_from_packages(self)` (Línea 509): Try to find the root package that is not a PEP 420 namespace

#### `def find_package_path(name, package_dir, root_dir)` (Línea 577)
- **Propósito:** Given a package name, return the path where it should be found on
disk, considering the ``package_dir`` option.

>>> path = find_package_path("my.pkg", {"": "root/is/nested"}, ".")
>>> path.replace(os.sep, "/")
'./root/is/nested/my/pkg'

>>> path = find_package_path("my.pkg", {"my": "root/is/nested"}, ".")
>>> path.replace(os.sep, "/")
'./root/is/nested/pkg'

>>> path = find_package_path("my.pkg", {"my.pkg": "root/is/nested"}, ".")
>>> path.replace(os.sep, "/")
'./root/is/nested'

>>> path = find_package_path("other.pkg", {"my.pkg": "root/is/nested"}, ".")
>>> path.replace(os.sep, "/")
